topics.label: Course introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their systemic limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer treatment modalities and the clinical limitations arising from their non-specific toxicity to healthy tissues.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how intrinsic molecular defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and repair deficiencies, can be selectively exploited for therapy.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinase signaling and managing therapeutic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting oncogene addiction and the mechanisms through which tumors evolve drug resistance and dependency.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on utilizing engineered monoclonal antibodies to target tumor surface markers and deliver cytotoxic payloads directly to cancer cells.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the evidence for immune surveillance and examine therapeutic approaches that stimulate or engineer T cells to eradicate tumors.

topics.label: Current challenges, future directions, and ethical dilemmas in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address overarching challenges in cancer treatment, including tumor heterogeneity, shifting epidemiological trends, and the clinical dilemmas of balancing efficacy with patient quality of life.
